title: Largest 1-Bordered Square
summary: In a 2D grid of zeros and ones, determine the count of elements in the largest square subgrid where all the border elements are ones, or return zero if no such subgrid exists.
statement: In a 2D grid of zeros and ones, determine the count of elements in the largest square subgrid where all the border elements are ones, or return zero if no such subgrid exists.
constraints: Return the area, not side length.
hints: Precompute consecutive ones ending at every cell from the left and above.
Treat each one as a possible bottom-right corner.
Try side lengths bounded by its left/up runs and verify the opposite top and left borders.
Every candidate border is checked in constant time after the DP preprocessing.
editorial: Every candidate border is checked in constant time after the DP preprocessing.

tests.explanation: The outer border is all ones, so the area is nine.
All four cells form a bordered square of area four.
